chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jameela, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin your day with goodness, and dictate upon your preservers (the Two recording Angels) goodness at its beginning and goodness at its end; He will forgive you for what is between that, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.حَفَظَتِكُمْ: Your preservers (referring to the two recording angels, Kiraman Katibin)

ai.seo_question: How can one seek forgiveness for daily sins through conscious remembrance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual efficacy of initiating the day with conscious affirmation of goodness, directing the recording angels (Hafazat) to favorably record one's state. This practice of 'filling' the day with good intentions serves as a means for divine forgiveness of intervening sins, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between human agency and angelic recording in daily spiritual life. The instruction underscores the importance of starting with *khayr* (goodness) to ensure a positive spiritual trajectory throughout the day.
